newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Jan 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A new strategic alliance between Coca-Cola Amatil and Telstra, to be announced today, may mean people will be able to buy cans of Coke from pay telephones within five years in a plan based on the 140,000 payphones and soft drink vending machines that CCA and Telstra already have between them in Australia. Page 1.

After finding that Melbourne Metropolitan Fire Brigade firefighters spend less than five per cent of their time attending emergencies or false alarms, a report by KPMG Management Consulting, set to be widely read across Australia, has suggested some Melbourne fire stations should be contracted out, so that firefighters can take on a wider emergency role. Page 2.

Acting Prime Minister and Federal National Party Leader Tim Fischer has been criticised by his Queensland counterparts for publicly floating a model for change to the constitution. National Party Senate Leader Ron Boswell said yesterday Fischer's plan was unhelpful, did not reflect party policy, and had no support in the bush. Page 3.

The Industrial Relations Court has criticised the senior management of the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission over their sacking of a staff member last year. The Court ordered the HREOC to pay A$26,957 to a sacked indigenous development office employed on a fixed term basis rather than as a permanent public servant, after deciding the employee's dismissal was not defensible as management had failed to consult with the employee. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The president of the Northern Territory branch of the Australian Medical Association, Chris Wake - one of the investigators of a High Court challenge to the Territory's controversial euthanasia laws - yesterday warned of an "open door" on euthanasia as Phillip Nitschke, the doctor of the first two people to die under the laws, renewed calls to make the legislation easier to access. Page 1.

In a thinly-veiled swipe at the leadership capabilities of National Party Leader and Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer, National Senate Leader Ron Boswell publicly criticised Fischer's recent comments on the republic, saying his comments had led to confuson about the party's roots and its leader's commitment to existing party policy opposing a republic. Page 1.

Hopes were rising yesterday for Briton Tony Bullimore and Frenchman Thierry Dubois, two lone yachtsmen stricken in the Southern Ocean - a long-range RAAF Orion aircraft re-established contact yesterday with Dubois, who was said to be "comfortable" in a drfting liferaft, and there were indications Bullimore may be alive in the hull of his upturned yacht. Page 1.

Speaking to the Bar Association of India in New Delhi on Monday, High Court Justice Michael Kirby added to the debate about judicial method by saying judicial activism for today's judge is inescapable, but in unchecked activism there are dangers, including for the courts themselves. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A confidential analysis of this year's HSC results has found New South Wales' high-profile specialist schools performed well below average, Government co-educational high schools have struggled to match the performance of single sex schools, and schools in the Catholic school system have again outperformed Government schools. Page 1.

Former electronics group AWA is considering bidding up to A$750 million, which it will raise by issuing new shares, to buy 75 per cent of the New South Wales Totaliser Agency Board (TAB) - a move that would allow the public to invest in the off-course gambling agency through the sharemarket. Page 1.

Frenchman Thierry Dubois spent last night clinging to a liferaft in the Southern Ocean amid cold weather and storms, and was expected to be reached by an Australian rescue ship at midnight. The lone yachtsman was faring better than fellow yachtsman, Englshman Tony Bullimore, who is also stranded in the ocean, yet his whereabouts are unknown. Page 1.

A senior officer in the New South Wales Department of Juvenile Justice has been accused of committing sexual assaults against a detainee 16 years ago. The 31-year-old man, Shane Hathaway of Penrith, claims that while in custody the officer drugged and asaulted him and that his complaints were ignored with the officer subsequently being promoted. This accusation follows on last month's New South Wales Ombudsman report that the juvenile justice system failed to meet international standards in the treatment of detainees. Page 3.
THE AGE

National Party Senate Leader Ron Boswell led a revolt within the party yesterday over Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer's move to push the party's position on the republican debate away from support for the monarchy. Boswell said Fischer's entry into the debate last week was unhelpful and had no official status. Page A1.

As the Victorian National Party split further yesterday over the future of Essendon Airport, Senator Julian McGauran cited new figures that contradict Transport Department evidence that the airport is struggling, and urged rural communities to fight for the site. Page A1.

Taking advantage of longer daylight hours, the commander of the frigate HMAS Adelaide, Captain Raydon Gates, is expected to launch a Seahawk helicopter tonight to try and rescue French yachtsman Thierry Dubois from a liferaft in freezing seas 1400 nautical miles south-west of Perth. Page A1.

New Austin Medical Centre evidence shows that open-heart surgery cases once considered urgent are automatically being classified by at least one hospital as semi-urgent, with 115 cardiac patients on category two (semi-urgent) in November, including 73 patents listed for more than 90 days. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
